question: Chest X-ray (CXR) is the first-line imaging investigation in a patient presenting with breathlessness and suspected cardiac failure, because it is fast, widely available, and can simultaneously assess cardiac size, pulmonary vasculature, and lung fields.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This statement is true. CXR is the first-line imaging in suspected heart failure because it provides rapid, comprehensive information about cardiac size, pulmonary venous pressure, and oedema pattern. Echocardiography is the definitive functional study that follows.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. CXR is the logical first step: it assesses cardiomegaly (CTR >0.5), vascular redistribution, interstitial and alveolar oedema, and pleural effusions — all in a single bedside study. Echocardiography then follows to assess systolic and diastolic function.
